rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
problems: directional label on a comparable share: 31 of 115 stories (27%)
rows.text:
People struggle most with old photos they only vaguely remember, across three kinds. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
- Among memories like people, trips, or events, 31 of 115 stories (27%) say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
- Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
- Among receipts, documents, and notes, 8 of 21 stories say the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
One post fits the feeling: “Went to find a funny old photo … and all I found was pain and trauma” [[story|c506bc4e0665d97093cc262fb824188a445b19f8:0]].
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a simple summary you can share?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably tell what people remember, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on that point to rely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]]

People often recall what was in the photo, like the main subject or photo type. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:photo_type@photo_class:_all]]
Some remember when it was taken, like the year, and some remember who was in it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:_all]]
A few remember objects or an activity in the shot. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:objects@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:activity@photo_class:_all]]
One person wrote they searched the “words on the posters” to find the photo. [[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown by place or event instead?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.text:
People most often forgot when the photo was taken. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] They also forgot the date or year. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]] Some forgot where it was taken, like the exact place or venue name. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]] A few even forgot whether it was a photo, video, or screenshot, or which app or account it came from. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:source:core]] One person wrote they had “a photo of nagito’s bare ass” saved but not the timing, showing fuzzy memory of when. [[story|6b5b098ff4054dff58acb46b2aff57a17fe9f25a:0]][[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick recap sorted by when, where, and what?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple word or object they remember, like bicycle or vomit. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]][[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]] Many stories say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos, in 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Some people still find the photo even with vague memory, in 38 of 115 stories (33%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]] Others skip the search box and scroll or look elsewhere, in 9 of 115 stories (8%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:_all]] One post says “I just search Google Photos for ‘bicycle’” [[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]]. One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples by the words people tried?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.text:
Often, yes. In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] 
Some people still found their photo: in 38 of 115 stories (33%), nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] 
One person said search showed “too many photos with no dog or pictures with ‘hot-dog’.” [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]] 
One limit is that these are public posts, not a share of users or searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of other common reasons people couldn’t find a photo?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The stories do not contain financial or revenue data for Google Photos and cannot answer revenue questions. These are public posts about trying to find a photo; they cannot tell us annual revenue. To answer this, we would need audited financial statements or official company reports.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: There is no measurable count of monthly users in the stories; they contain only public stories about finding photos and no usage telemetry, so they cannot answer monthly active user questions. These are public posts about trying to find a photo, they cannot answer this, and data from product telemetry or a representative usage panel would be needed.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
These are public posts about trying to find a photo. They cannot answer the success rate for searches from vague memories. To answer that, you would need usage data that tracks attempts and outcomes across all users.

*What kind of data access do you have?*

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split
rows.text:
We cannot tell if Android users struggle more than iPhone users, because the posts do not reliably say which phone people use. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What we can say is that many stories describe trouble with what they typed or what was shown: 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
Some stories say the photo was already gone: 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
Others say people never used the search box: 9 of 115 stories (8%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
One person wrote it “took me forever to find it” [[story|4217b5d02ba957a72904fa796a4bd54327cf19d2:0]]. 

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Do you want the same breakdown for stories where people knew the exact photo?*

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.gap: the stories were not compared across time, so there is no before-and-after
rows.text:
These stories cannot show change over time, so there is no before-and-after for Ask Photos. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What people most often wrote about, in 31 of 115 stories (27%), was that search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

Some people did find the photo: 38 of 115 stories (33%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

One person said it worked — “they pop right up there!!” [[story|14ed655bd0a022582467843de12eb960c2bf90a8:0]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to compare this with stories about an exact photo?*

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
problems: directional label on a comparable share: 31 of 115 stories (27%)
rows.gap: the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.text:
These stories cannot say whether Apple Photos search is better than Google Photos search. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

People often said the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos, in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
Even so, nothing went wrong in 38 of 115 stories (33%) — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
One person said they “instantly find the image I want” in Google Photos. [[story|b7113e3689e0674b9cd8b089fb3bcd093e40d3eb:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of what went wrong when search missed?*

rows.question: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.restated: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about how far down the results they went — 2 of 115 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
These stories cannot tell us how deep people scroll, because few public posts say how far down they went — 2 of 115 stories do — so this is left for interviews with real users. [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]

Some went a few scrolls before deciding. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]]
Others went all the way down. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:_all]]
Only 2 of 115 stories say anything about how far down the results they went. [[analysis_coverage|6.6]]
One limit is that these are public posts, not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick view of which problems show up before people decide to stop scrolling?*

rows.question: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.restated: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?

rows.text:
These stories cannot tell how often a wrong year acts as a hard filter, because few public posts say anything about the system discarded the photo because one detail was wrong — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users. [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]

A small mistake in a detail did not matter in 2 of 115 stories (2%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=soft_ok@photo_class:_all]]
Adding more words made the photo disappear in 1 of 115 stories (1%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]]
One person wrote “it says no results” when they added words. [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

These stories cannot tell us how many attempts people make before they give up, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on this point. [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]]

Some did only one try: 21 of 115 stories (18%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Some tried a few times over some minutes: 6 of 115 stories (5%), a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
A few kept at it for an hour or more: 3 of 115 stories (3%), a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
One person wrote “No matter how many times I look back at the photos, I can't find a shot” [[story|3f6c7b626f52b658b0c519881ff8cb6967208570:0]]

*Want a quick view of where their searches first went wrong?*
rows.text:
The stories cannot tell you all of this: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on how long they kept trying to rely on it. [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]

- In 21 of 115 stories (18%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, on how long they kept trying, the post says: one try. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]]
- In 6 of 115 stories (5%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, on how long they kept trying, the post says: a few tries over some minutes. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]]
- In 3 of 115 stories (3%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, on how long they kept trying, the post says: an hour or more. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|a8eaefe2e0199103bba08d2d1f34aad86d3267a5:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
problems: directional label on a comparable share: 31 of 115 stories (27%)
directional label on a comparable share: 20 of 115 stories (17%)
rows.text:
Most often, Ask Photos fails because the search does not understand what people type, or it shows the wrong photos — 31 of 115 stories (27%), a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
The next common reason is that the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else — 20 of 115 stories (17%), a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
One person said, “I can't find some of my pictures and videos.” [[story|2f6fb3f2ee87b1ba4b06a4e3786f964394e1af14:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick chart of the main reasons?*

rows.question: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.restated: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
withheld: unverifiable quote: text search … and be disappointed.
rows.draft:
Fix search understanding first. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] It is where 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered first go wrong, and it is the one problem with enough stories to rank. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Apply AI to interpret simple cues, link them to people, places, and time, and strengthen concept and entity indexing. [[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:intelligence_needed]] Deleted or elsewhere comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%), and better search could not fix it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]] One person said “text search … and be disappointed.” [[story|b2358d9efca162742579284a99c00a353586c178:0]][[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:chain:evidence]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick sketch of what “interpret simple cues” could look like?*
rows.text:
- The problem — search did not understand or match what they typed — comes up in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 30 people. It is the one problem with enough stories to rank. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]]
- The problem — the photo was gone before anyone searched — deleted, never backed up, elsewhere — comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 20 people. Better search could not fix it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]]
- The problem — they never searched — scrolled the timeline or didn't know search could help — comes up in 9 of 115 stories (8%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 9 people. Too few stories to rank it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage3]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|beebc7898400af1a0cc9f1ea6c04d016e3940312:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: What share of utility-photo stories end with the person giving up?
rows.restated: What proportion of stories about practical photos end with the person giving up?
rows.text:
4 of 115 stories (3%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered end with them giving up. [[analysis_crosstab|core.outcome=abandoned_without_fallback@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
In 50 of 216 stories (23%) about a photo the person knew exactly, or one already gone, they gave up. [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.outcome=abandoned_without_fallback@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:adjacent]]  
Some people also gave up and got it another way in 6 of 216 stories (3%). [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.outcome=abandoned_with_fallback@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:adjacent]]  
One post shows the tone of giving up: “I checked every where but not found.” [[story|d61372a756937f20e42f4a95ba72726b5b136b29:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a split just for receipts and documents?*

rows.question: What share of stories about photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons fail at search?
rows.restated: What proportion of stories about photos that are kept for both sentimental and practical reasons experienced a search failure (i.e., their finding the photo journey first went wrong before the final 'nothing went wrong' outcome)?
rows.gap: none of the stories is about photos kept both as memories and for the information in them, so nothing can be said about them
rows.text:
Nothing in these stories can say what share fails for photos kept both as memories and for their information. [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]

For photos kept as memories, 17 of 48 stories (35%) say nothing went wrong — they found the photo — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
For photos kept for the information in them, 6 of 21 stories say nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:utility]]
One person wrote that search “doesn't work well at all” and struggled to find “cheese” they had photographed as notes. [[story|dc2535631942cc6b5a068698bf80431a03d4c971:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want figures for what went wrong first, by each kind of photo?*

rows.question: How many core stories are there, and from how many different people?
rows.restated: How many stories about a vaguely remembered photo are there, and from how many different people?
rows.text:
There are 115 stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered — the stories most answers here rest on — told by 109 people. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Another 216 stories are counted separately, where the person knew exactly which photo they wanted, or it was already gone. [[analysis_funnel|stories:adjacent]]
One post shows the kind of struggle people wrote about: “y’all have no idea how many bill hader pictures i had to scroll through on my google photos” [[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick recap of how those 115 stories played out?*

rows.question: How many core stories first go wrong because search did not understand or match what was typed?
rows.restated: How many stories about a vaguely remembered photo had their first failure at the step where search did not understand or match what the user typed?
rows.text:
31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered first went wrong because the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]  
Among photos kept as memories (people, trips, events), 13 of 48 stories (27%) say this — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say this — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
“I put one in there on purpose to test a bunch of search words and nothings working.” [[story|4f97934e36516780fd57de1c6d42d5da089277a5:0]]

*Want a quick view of counts for document-like photos too?*

rows.question: And how does that split by kind of photo?
rows.restated: How often does finding the photo first go wrong at each step, split by kind of photo (sentimental, practical, both, unclear)?
rows.text:
Across kinds of photo, the same two things come up first: they either found it, or search misunderstood them. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]]  
Among memories (people, trips, events), 17 of 48 stories (35%) found the photo — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]]  
In those memories, 13 of 48 stories (27%) said search misunderstood or showed wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]  
Where the post did not say why the photo was kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) found it — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:unclear]]  
There, 15 of 46 stories (33%) said search misunderstood or showed wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]]  
For information photos, counts only: gone already in 8 of 21, found in 6 of 21, memory too faint in 4 of 21, search misunderstood in 3 of 21. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]]  
One person wrote “returned way too many images of my shop” [[story|0ef3821f2d59998617a4b53f428fd49c9a22d2ff:0]].  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want the same split for not using the search box first?*

rows.question: Does that differ for utility photos?
rows.restated: Do people searching for practical photos (like receipts) start their searches differently than people searching for memory photos (sentimental)?
rows.gap: only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given
rows.draft:
We cannot give percentages for utility photos; only 21 stories are about receipts, documents, or notes — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

Yes, it differs a bit. In stories about utility photos, 3 of 21 say the first try was a single word. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
And 2 of 21 say they started with several keywords. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
For memory photos, 11 of 48 stories (23%) say a single word — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:sentimental]]
One person looking for a receipt typed “scrap” and got many shop images: “returned way too many images of my shop.” [[story|0ef3821f2d59998617a4b53f428fd49c9a22d2ff:0]]

*Want side‑by‑side counts for utility vs. “reason not said”?*
rows.text:
The stories cannot tell you all of this: only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

- In 3 of 21 stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, among photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes), on what they typed first, the post says: a single word. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.text:
People say the search did not understand their words, so “receipt” showed nothing or the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One person wrote, “I couldn't find the receipt for my laptop, 'receipt' returned nothing.” [[story|probe-inj-04]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Another said searching “scrap” for a scrap receipt brought “way too many images” from their shop. [[story|0ef3821f2d59998617a4b53f428fd49c9a22d2ff:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Some also say the photo might be gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples of terms people tried when “receipt” failed?*

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Most often, the search misunderstands what people type, or shows the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] For stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, this happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One post puts it simply: “'dog park' never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter.” [[story|probe-inj-06]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Sometimes the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else — in 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
